tests.what: A static load test with strain gauges and a dial gauge, loaded in steps of 500 N, 1000 N, 1500 N and 2000 N

gauges.why: the governing point, where the answer is decided
gauges.note: the stress changes 26% under a 3 mm grid here, so use a 1 mm grid or read the gauge as an average over its length

gauges.why: a calm spot on the main load path, where a gauge checks the overall stiffness without fighting a steep gradient
the point that moves most, for a dial gauge or a displacement sensor

tests.why: It supplies the comparison with tests that V&V 20 needs, at the point the decision rests on and up to the design load.

tests.what: A strain gauge at (-34, 0, 29.5), where the rigid attachment puts its peak
tests.why: With a rigid attachment the peak sits here at 55 MPa, and with the distributed one Wobbl predicts 18.1 MPa at the same spot. A reading here tells which idealization the real assembly is closer to, a choice that moves the answer more than any input scatter.

test: Measure the 2000 N load in service, with a load cell or a strain gauged link
tests.what: Measure the 2000 N load in service, with a load cell or a strain gauged link.
tests.why: Knowing the load exactly removes about 61% of the variance of the safety factor, taking its standard deviation from 0.173 to about 0.108.

test: Tensile test coupons from the same lot, casting or print settings, measuring the yield strength (yield)
tests.what: Tensile test coupons from the same lot, casting or print settings, measuring the yield strength (yield).
tests.why: Knowing the yield exactly removes about 39% of the variance of the safety factor, taking its standard deviation from 0.173 to about 0.135.
tests.how_many: At least 10 coupons, since the uncertainty in the lot mean falls with the square root of their number, to a third of the scatter at 9.

replace.test: a static proof test at the design load
replace.why: the readings are synthetic, the failure probability is not small enough to stand on the model alone, credibility factors are short of their goals

replace.test: strain surveys of later design variants
replace.why: no validated survey exists to carry over
Wobbl's strength model is linear elastic and stops at the first yield, so it says nothing about how the part fails after that
they measure the inputs the model rests on
this run is a static strength study and does not model them

rule: the validation test whenever a validation factor is short of its goal, the discriminating gauge whenever the model form is, and input measurements by first order Sobol index until they cover 80% of the variance measuring could remove
headline: 4 tests would most reduce the risk, in this order, a validation test, a gauge where the idealizations differ, a service load measurement and material coupons.
